The correct probability is 2/17, so none of the three solutions is right.

**Correct value.** Let P(n) be the probability that Michael and James ever battle together, starting from n players (n ≡ 1 mod 3). In one round, the chance both are chosen is C(n−2,2)/C(n,4) = 12/(n(n−1)). The chance both survive the round without meeting is (n−3)(n−4)/(n(n−1)) (exactly one chosen and that one wins, or neither chosen), and then n−3 players remain. So

P(n) = 12/(n(n−1)) + [(n−3)(n−4)/(n(n−1))]·P(n−3), with P(4) = 1.

Multiplying by n(n−1) and setting Q(n) = n(n−1)P(n) gives Q(n) = Q(n−3) + 12, with Q(4) = 12. For n = 34 there are 10 steps, so Q(34) = 132 and

P(34) = 132/(34·33) = 2/17.

Check: for n = 7 the recurrence gives 4/7, which matches a direct computation.

**Why each solution fails.**
- Solution 1 ends with "79", which is not a valid probability for this problem.
- Solution 2 derives a recurrence in the right spirit but miscounts the "exactly one chosen" case as C(n−3,3) instead of C(n−2,3). Its final value, 18571639447/176405028800 ≈ 0.10528, is wrong.
- Solution 3 uses the heuristic 2/g = 1/2 without justification, and 1/2 is not the answer.

CHOICE: NONE
